**Visual analysis of the test image:**

- **Affected plant part**: Corn leaf sheath (cylindrical structure wrapping the stalk)
- **Key features**:
  - Small, dark brown to black, circular/oval lesions scattered across the tissue
  - Lesions appear distinct, slightly sunken, with dark centers
  - Background tissue is green/yellow-green, still largely healthy
  - Some marginal browning along the edges of the sheath

**Reasoning through candidates:**

- **Physoderma brown spot**: Causes small, round to oval, dark brown/black spots on leaves and leaf sheaths. Lesions on sheaths tend to be darker and more discrete. This matches very well.
- **Eyespot**: Small circular spots with tan centers and dark borders — centers here appear too dark, no tan center visible.
- **Holcus spot**: White to tan oval spots with brown borders — color doesn't match; these spots are dark.
- **Gray leaf spot**: Rectangular lesions parallel to veins — wrong shape.
- **Common rust**: Raised pustules — no pustules visible here.
- **Anthracnose leaf spot**: Can show dark lesions but typically on leaf blade with more irregular shapes.

The combination of small, dark, circular/oval discrete spots specifically on the leaf sheath tissue is the hallmark of **Physoderma brown spot** (caused by *Physoderma maydis*), which characteristically infects leaf sheaths with darker, more defined lesions than the paler spots seen on leaf blades.
